title: The Spider and the Wind

full_text:
Between two branches of a rosebush in a royal garden, a large garden spider spun an intricate, symmetrical web of delicate silk. When the morning dew caught the sunlight, the web sparkled like diamonds strung upon silver cords.

Puffed up with immense pride, the spider strutted to the center of his web, looked down upon the worker ants crawling in the dust, and boasted aloud:

'Look upon my palace! I spin my own architecture out of my own substance, suspended in the air like a celestial bridge! Neither the King of Persia nor the architects of Rome have ever built a palace so geometric, delicate, and radiant!'

A passing honeybee buzzed: 'Your web is beautiful, neighbor, but remember that it hangs upon slender twigs; do not boast until you have tested its strength against the storm.'

The spider scoffed: 'My silk is stronger than iron cables! Let the elements challenge my genius!'

At that moment, the autumn north wind began to blow. A gentle gust of wind swept through the garden; the rose branches swayed, and with a single soft sigh, the delicate spiderweb was torn into shreds and scattered like mist into the grass!

The spider was tumbled into the dirt, bruised and shivering beneath a dry leaf, weeping over his ruined masterpiece.

The humble ant stopped beside him and said: 'He who builds his palace out of pride will find that a passing breeze turns his empire to nothing. Build upon solid ground, and let your works speak without boasting.'
moral: Boastful arrogance in frail works of vanity is swept away in an instant by the breath of nature.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Spider and the Wind"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
